messages.text: I recorded this explanation in OBS today. Please turn the recordings in raw/ into a polished landscape educational video, keeping the complete explanation while removing failed starts, repetition, and unnecessary dead time. Use the project's monochrome visual style, improve the voice with local AI cleanup, and add explanatory motion graphics where they make the idea easier to follow. Use the screen and camera footage appropriately. Deliver the finished 1920 × 1080 video, timed captions, and editable project here for me to review. Don't post it to any social platform.

I’ll inspect the recordings and project guidance, then build the edit around the complete explanation. I’m using the video editing, video inspection, motion graphics, and writing skills for the cut, visuals, captions, and review notes.

The separate screen recording is distorted, but the screen view in the OBS program recording is usable. The camera recording is clean. I’ll recover screen footage from the program recording and use the separate camera for the presenter shots.

I also found four program audio tracks, including a silent one. I’m comparing the speech tracks and measuring their offsets before making cuts.

The explanation centers on the “lethal trifecta”: one agent reading untrusted content, accessing private data, and communicating externally. I’m keeping the proposal anecdote, the email example, and the full safer-workflow explanation, including your qualification about human approval.

The edit will use light monochrome graphics to show those permissions converging, then separate email classification from deterministic code and approval. The repeated openings and abandoned sentences can come out without losing those points.

The cut is about 3½ minutes, down from 6½ minutes. Local DeepFilterNet cleanup reduced the quiet background noise by about 19.5 dB in the comparison passage, with little change to speech level. I’ve kept matched dry and cleaned excerpts for your review.

I’m now assembling the graphics and checking the edited transcript for clipped words or awkward joins. Captions will follow the finished cut, with a local review page for playback.

I’m continuing with the render and final checks. The graphics are laid out, and the edited voice track is assembled. Next I’m checking caption timing, screen readability, and the camera cuts in the exported video.
